source.title: GCSAM: Gradient Centralized Sharpness Aware Minimization
source.authors: Mohamed Hassan; Aleksandar Vakanski; Bo-Yu Zhang; M. Xian

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including its appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study builds GCSAM on SAM’s sharpness-minimization finding, then evaluates its own optimizer. It does not test the claim versions’ specified comparisons or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracies for Adam, SAM, GCSAM and other SAM variants, but those optimizer comparisons do not match a version’s specified test. The COVID-19 loss-landscape figures and their textual description report a sharpness-related measurement, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. No results on random-label memorization, width sweeps, CNN versus fully connected models, large batches, dropout, magnitude-aware perturbations, or memorized-example removal are reported.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization premise to develop GCSAM and evaluates its optimizer performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, rank generalization gaps against alternative measures, or perform any other claim version's comparison. Adam versus SAM variants does not establish the adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that GCSAM improves test accuracy over Adam and SAM across their datasets and reduces training time relative to SAM. Their claim of outperforming every tested SAM variant needs qualification: on COVID-19 with ViT, GCSAM ties ASAM at 82.5%. GCSAM also takes longer than Adam in all reported COVID-19 comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a modified SAM ascent step using gradient centralization; its experiments compare optimizers on CIFAR-10 and medical image datasets, not the specified claim-version tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture vary across the reported experiments; no sensitivity analysis of the claim’s specified measures is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 describes ResNet50 trained on COVID-19 with GCSAM as having the flattest landscape and Adam the sharpest, using two Gaussian perturbation directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this ResNet50 COVID-19 experiment, GCSAM produces a qualitatively flatter loss landscape than Adam and SAM.

record.problems: The loss-landscape comparison is qualitative and figure-based, with no reported uncertainty or quantified relation to the train-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: Optimizer test-accuracy and speed comparisons in Tables 1–3 were not extracted because the study's proposed GCSAM method is evaluated for its own performance, and those comparisons do not measure a version's specified behavior. Table 3 compares Adam, SAM and SAM variants, but not the specified Adam-versus-SGD or momentum-SGD comparison.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and training recipes, including chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test-error trends when widening networks beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, including tuning, weight-decay, and optimizer-switching conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes from adapting the training recipe.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking performance relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Tables 1–3 are already declared in rows_left_out and do not supply the missing comparisons required by any version. The appendix's generalization bound concerns the proposed method; it does not test V7's empirical correlation or comparative ranking claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning comparisons; Adam is compared with SAM and its variants.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking of train-test gaps; the paper presents loss-landscape plots but does not test that measure or correlate it with gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
